trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ
trials.population: Adults with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) Score
trials.results_summary: Donanemab showed a borderline significant slowing of cognitive decline on the iADRS compared to placebo (p=0.042) and a highly significant reduction in amyloid plaques. Secondary cognitive endpoints generally failed to reach statistical significance.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) (Overall Population)
trials.results_summary: Donanemab significantly slowed clinical decline on the iADRS and CDR-SB compared to placebo over 76 weeks, successfully confirming the Phase 2 findings.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3
trials.primary_endpoint: Time to Clinical Progression of Composite Endpoint as Measured by Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR)

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 4
trials.primary_endpoint: Percentage of Participants With Complete Amyloid Plaque Clearance on Florbetapir Positron Emission Tomography (PET)
trials.results_summary: Donanemab demonstrated superior brain amyloid plaque clearance compared to aducanumab.

related_evidence.description: Mintun et al., Phase 2 TRAILBLAZER-ALZ results in NEJM
Sims et al., Phase 3 TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 results in JAMA
FDA approval of Kisunla (donanemab-azbt) for early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence supporting donanemab in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease is robust, successfully translating the initial borderline clinical efficacy seen in the Phase 2 TRAILBLAZER-ALZ trial into definitive clinical benefit in Phase 3. While the Phase 2 document appropriately highlights a highly significant biomarker response (amyloid reduction) alongside only marginal statistical significance on the primary iADRS endpoint and non-significant secondary cognitive measures, the larger Phase 3 TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 trial subsequently met all primary and secondary endpoints. This successful replication validates the Phase 2 findings and drug mechanism, culminating in FDA approval in July 2024. Ongoing studies (like TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3) continue to explore its efficacy in earlier, preclinical stages.
